assumptions: airline_fuel_cost: Everything the model does not include stays at its baseline: fuel consumption, other costs, traffic, capacity, fares (apart from the stated pass-through) and financing.
airline_fuel_cost: Fuel is consumed evenly through the year: each month uses one twelfth of the annual volume, and annual revenue and costs accrue evenly.
airline_fuel_cost: The fuel bill is consumption × the benchmark jet fuel price × the exchange rate. Taxes, fees and supplier margins that do not follow the benchmark are outside the model.

airline_fuel_cost: Scenario changes are step changes: they take effect in the start month and last for the stated duration (to the end of the horizon unless one is set), after which the changed variables return to their baselines. Every change in a run shares this timing.

airline_fuel_cost: Jet fuel responds to crude oil with a constant elasticity β after a lag: ln(jet fuel) changes by β × ln(1 + crude change). With β = 1 the refining margin stays a constant proportion of the price.
airline_fuel_cost: Hedged fuel pays the baseline US-dollar price until the hedges expire; the exchange rate is not hedged; hedges are not rolled over.
airline_fuel_cost: Fares recover a fixed share of the change in fuel cost after a lag, for rises and falls alike, and passenger demand does not respond.
airline_fuel_cost: The exchange rate affects the fuel bill only: other dollar costs and any dollar revenue are outside the model.
airline_fuel_cost: Crude-to-jet-fuel elasticity (β) = 1 elasticity (dimensionless) (default)
airline_fuel_cost: Crude-to-jet-fuel lag = 1 months (entered)
airline_fuel_cost: Hedge ratio = 40 % (entered)
airline_fuel_cost: Hedge cover = 6 months (entered)
airline_fuel_cost: Fare pass-through = 50 % (entered)
airline_fuel_cost: Fare pass-through lag = 2 months (entered)
floating_rate_interest: Everything the model does not include stays at its baseline: the amount of debt (no repayments or new borrowing), fixed-rate debt, operating profit and other income.

floating_rate_interest: Floating-rate loans reprice by the stated share of the benchmark change after the stated delay, then keep that rate while the change lasts. Interest accrues evenly: each month carries one twelfth of the annual rate.
floating_rate_interest: The benchmark change is taken as given. RUMIN does not predict policy rates.

floating_rate_interest: Scenario changes are step changes: they take effect in the start month and last for the stated duration (to the end of the horizon unless one is set), after which the changed variables return to their baselines. Every change in a run shares this timing.
floating_rate_interest: Debt linked to US rates is stated in the reporting currency at today's exchange rate; exchange-rate movements on it are not modelled here.
floating_rate_interest: Repo pass-through = 100 % (default)
floating_rate_interest: Repo repricing delay = 3 months (entered)
floating_rate_interest: US-rate pass-through = 100 % (default)
floating_rate_interest: US-rate repricing delay = 0 months (default)
fx_exposure: Everything the model does not include stays at its baseline: the US-dollar amounts, volumes, prices in every currency, other costs and financing.
fx_exposure: US-dollar revenue and costs accrue evenly through the year: each month carries one twelfth.
fx_exposure: Dollar amounts are converted at the month's exchange rate. Dollar prices, volumes and demand do not respond to the exchange rate.

fx_exposure: Scenario changes are step changes: they take effect in the start month and last for the stated duration (to the end of the horizon unless one is set), after which the changed variables return to their baselines. Every change in a run shares this timing.
fx_exposure: Hedges fix the baseline exchange rate for the hedged share during the first months of cover, then expire; they are not rolled over. Revenue and cost hedges are separate.
fx_exposure: Only amounts invoiced or paid in US dollars are exposed. Costs another model in the same scenario already converts must be left out of the US-dollar costs.
fx_exposure: Revenue hedge ratio = 0 % (default)
fx_exposure: Cost hedge ratio = 0 % (default)
fx_exposure: Hedge cover = 0 months (default)

chain.text: Share of exposure paths through each variable
Concentrated at or above 50 % of paths

assumptions: USD/INR exchange rate affects costs of Aerisca Airways: Aircraft leases and maintenance are commonly priced in U.S. dollars, so a weaker rupee raises an Indian airline's costs in rupees.
Jet fuel price (U.S. Gulf Coast) affects costs of Air transport: Fuel is typically one of the largest operating costs for airlines.

Brent crude oil price influences Jet fuel price (U.S. Gulf Coast): Jet fuel is refined from crude oil, so benchmark jet fuel prices generally move with crude prices. Refining margins (the crack spread) cause the two to diverge at times.

U.S. effective federal funds rate influences USD/INR exchange rate: Higher U.S. policy rates can strengthen the dollar and draw portfolio capital away from emerging markets, adding depreciation pressure on the rupee. The link is unstable and often dominated by other factors, hence 'weak'.
limitations: A share of relationships, not of costs or revenue.
Supply and credit relationships say nothing about size or terms.
